text:
Ana: heads-up — woke up to noisy evictions in us-west last night. Shared-hosted nodepool got aggressively scaled down and a bunch of tenant pods hit Pending+Evicted around 03:12 UTC. Thinking we should formalize split pools + stricter netpols. @Lia any recollection of what triggered scale-down?
Ken: saw the same, looks like a short CPU spike from a maint job then CA scaled down soon after. scale-down-unneeded-time is 10m but we have bursty short jobs, so timing mismatch. logs attached to incident thread.
Matt: fwiw, tenant isolation via nodepool labels + taints has worked for latency-sensitive workloads. e.g. taint: `dedicated-pool=true:NoSchedule` + namespace tolerations. but that increases cost.
Lia: agree. also caution on NetworkPolicy: when we locked down egress recently we accidentally blocked metrics export for a hosted tenant — that caused a bunch of liveness failures and then compounding evictions. ops-oncall had to whitelist s3 & prometheus endpoints.
infra-bot: alert: cluster-autoscaler/us-west returned scaleDown failed 3 times between 03:08-03:15. reason: nodes not empty (pods have localStorage).
Ana: that's the loop. node drains failing --> CA retries --> partial downscale + new pods pending --> pod preemption/eviction. Two mitigations I want to discuss: 1) split pools (hosted fast-burst pool + dedicated reserved pools) 2) soft-eviction policy / grace for drains for tenants with critical KV workloads.
Ken: proposal for nodepool config snippet I tested locally:
```yaml
apiVersion: infrastructure.redwood.io/v1
kind: NodePool
metadata:
  name: hosted-burst-us-west
spec:
  labels:
    pool-type: hosted-burst
  taints:
    - key: pool-type
      value: hosted-burst
      effect: NoSchedule
  autoscaling:
    minSize: 2
    maxSize: 20
    scaleDownUnneededTime: 15m
```
Matt: increase `scaleDownUnneededTime` and `scaleDownUtilizationThreshold` for burst pools. For dedicated pools keep small minSize and pin by affinity so CA doesn't touch them unless we explicitly allow.
Lia: network policy checklist if we split pools:
- allow cross-namespace DNS + kubelet + cni plugin flows
- allow egress to telemetry S3/prometheus endpoints
- allow hostPath/localStorage shutdown hooks to finish (or eviction grace)
ops-oncall: adding: make sure our CNI doesn't drop health-check traffic during pod migration. When we apply per-tenant netpols we should test drain scenarios in a staging AZ.
Ana: action items: 
- Ken to prototype `hosted-burst` pool yaml and run chaos-drain tests (due: 2d)
- Lia to produce minimal netpol template with telemetry whitelists (due: 3d)
- Matt to draft CA tuning doc (scale down thresholds + resourceLimits) and cost delta estimate for split pools (due: EOW)
- ops-oncall to add drain+netpol test to runbook and gating job
Anyone opposed to starting with a single AZ pilot before multi-az roll? :thumbsup:
Ken: +1 from me. Will spin up pilot cluster tomorrow.
Matt: +1. I'll run cost sims with current usage traces.
infra-bot: note: created task #INF-842 on infra backlog for CA tuning and pilot setup.
ops-oncall: I'll coordinate staging tests. tagging @Lia for the netpol draft.
Ana: cool — let's keep this tight. If we see edge cases during pilot we'll iterate. :rocket:
